rules.title: offset_of! signature
rules.statement: `offset_of!(Type, field)` requires both a type argument and a field name; either missing is a compile error.

rules.title: offset_of! requires a struct type
rules.statement: The type argument of `offset_of!` must resolve to a struct or zoned-struct type; otherwise it is a compile error. The named struct must be known.

rules.title: offset_of! yields a compile-time i64 byte offset
rules.statement: `offset_of!(T, f)` evaluates to an `i64` constant equal to the byte offset of field `f` within `T`'s layout, computed by sequentially laying out fields: each field is placed at the next position aligned up to its alignment, then advanced by its byte size. Result type is `i64`.
rules.divergence: Rust's offset_of! yields usize; Logos yields i64.

rules.title: offset_of! substitutes the type's generic args
rules.statement: When the struct is generic, the concrete type arguments of `T` are substituted into the field types before computing sizes/alignments, so `offset_of!` reflects the layout of the concrete instantiation.

rules.title: Alignment of unsized tail fields
rules.statement: Field alignment is min(byte_size,8) for sized fields (treating size-0 as align 1); an unsized `[T]` slice tail aligns to min(sizeof(T),8); an unsized `dyn` tail aligns to 8 (pointer width).

rules.title: cfg! evaluates to a bool
rules.statement: `cfg!(predicate)` evaluates the configuration predicate at compile time and yields a `bool` literal.

rules.title: vec! is a compiler builtin list-literal macro
rules.statement: `vec!(a, b, c)` / `vec![a, b, c]` constructs a `Vec` of its elements. A user-defined `vec` fn_macro/token_macro in scope overrides the builtin. With a known renderable element type E (from a `let v: Vec<E>` annotation), it lowers to a push-block `{ let mut __v: Vec<E> = vec_new::<E>(); __v.push(e0); …; __v }` (no Copy bound). Otherwise it lowers to `vec_from_arr([…])` (Copy-bound, inference-driven); `vec!()` empty lowers to `vec_new::<_>()`.

rules.title: line! / column! positional macros
rules.statement: `line!()` yields the current source line as `u32`; `column!()` yields `u32` 0 (columns are not tracked).
rules.divergence: column!() always returns 0 rather than the true column.

rules.title: file! / module_path! positional macros
rules.statement: `file!()` yields the current file path and `module_path!()` yields the current package name, each as a `&str` (`Slice<u8>`) string literal.

rules.title: include! splices a file as an expression
rules.statement: `include!("path")` reads the file at compile time and re-parses its contents as an expression spliced at the call site; only expression-position include! is supported (item-position is a compile error). Paths are resolved relative to the including file.
rules.divergence: Rust supports item-position include!; Logos supports only expression position.

rules.title: include_str! / include_bytes! embed file contents
rules.statement: `include_str!("path")` and `include_bytes!("path")` read the file at compile time (path relative to the including file) and yield its contents as a `&str` (`Slice<u8>`) literal; both forms collapse to the same representation since `str` is `Slice<u8>`. Unreadable files are a compile error.
rules.divergence: Rust's include_bytes! has type &[u8;N] distinct from &str; in Logos both are Slice<u8>.

rules.title: env! / option_env! read environment at compile time
rules.statement: `env!("VAR")` yields the value of environment variable VAR as a `&str` literal and is a compile error if unset; `option_env!("VAR")` yields the value or an empty `&str` if unset.
rules.divergence: option_env! returns an empty &str tombstone rather than Option<&str>.

rules.title: concat! string-literal concatenation
rules.statement: `concat!(a, b, …)` concatenates string, integer (decimal, suffix-stripped), and bool (`true`/`false`) literals at compile time into a single `&str` (`Slice<u8>`) literal. Non-literal args are a compile error. String escapes \n \t \r \\ \" \0 are decoded.
rules.divergence: Floats and char literals are not supported (Rust supports them).

rules.title: concat_bytes! byte-array concatenation
rules.statement: `concat_bytes!(…)` concatenates byte-string literals (`b"…"`), byte-char literals (`b'X'`), and integer literals in range 0..=255 (decimal/0x/0o/0b, suffix-allowed) at compile time, yielding a `[u8; N]` array literal. Out-of-range integers, dangling/unknown escapes, and unsupported args are compile errors.

rules.title: stringify! returns raw token text
rules.statement: `stringify!(…)` yields the raw source text between the parentheses as a `&str` (`Slice<u8>`) literal, without macro expansion of the contents.

rules.title: unreachable! / todo! / unimplemented! marker macros
rules.statement: `unreachable!`, `todo!`, and `unimplemented!` are thin wrappers around `panic!` with default prefix messages ("internal error: entered unreachable code", "not yet implemented", "not implemented"); with args they panic with `"<prefix>: {}"` filled by `format!(args)`. They type as `!` (Never) and are valid in any expression position.

rules.title: compile_error! emits a compile-time error
rules.statement: `compile_error!("msg")` takes one string-literal argument and emits that message as a compile-time error.

rules.title: matches! tests a pattern
rules.statement: `matches!(expr, pattern [if guard])` evaluates to `true` iff `expr` matches the pattern (with optional guard), else `false`; lowered to `match (expr) { pattern => true, _ => false }`. The first top-level comma splits expr from the pattern.

rules.title: dbg! prints and returns its argument
rules.statement: `dbg!(expr)` eprints `[file:line] expr = <Debug>` and evaluates to the value of `expr` (ownership passes through). `dbg!()` prints just `[file:line]` and yields `()`.
